{{Infobox person|gender={{ill|Male (gender)|ar|ذكر|diq|Lac|eo|Malino|es|Masculino|fr|Sexe masculin|ha|Namiji|id|Lelaki|kaj|A̱jjwa|new|बायचिं|pt|Masculino|scn|Masculiddu|sk|Mužské pohlavie|tok|mije kon|qid=Q6581097}}|children={{ill|Mizuha no Iratsume|qid=Q108044394}}; {{ill|Ishikijo-wake-no-Ō|qid=Q108044409}}; {{ill|Wakazusuiwake-no-Mikoto|qid=Q109930199}}|father={{ill|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850}}|mother={{ill|Kihobe|qid=Q109931034}}|relatives={{ill|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723}}; {{ill|Ojiwake no mikoto|ja|祖別命|zh|祖別命|qid=Q11620549}}; {{ill|Homutsuwake no Mikoto|ja|誉津別命|qid=Q11631423}}; {{ill|Prince Ikatarashihiko|ja|五十日足彦命|qid=Q11372186}}; {{ill|Prince Ikobayawake no Mikoto|ja|息速別命|zh|息速別命|qid=Q11492324}}; {{ill|Prince Inishikiirihiko|ja|五十瓊敷入彦命|qid=Q11372194}}; {{ill|Prince Tuburame|ja|円目王|qid=Q11394830}}; {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732}}}}

'''Iwattsukuwake no Mikoto''' (磐衝別命) (生没年不詳) is an ancient member of the imperial family of {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan}}, as transmitted in the {{ill|Kiki (Shinto)|ja|記紀|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q842308}} and other traditional records.

He is the tenth son of the 11th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Suinin Tennō}}, and was born to the daughter of Yamashiro Ōkuni Fuchisoku (山背大国不遅, also rendered as 山代大国之淵) and {{ill|Kamuhatotobe|ja|綺戸辺}} (かむはたとべ, 弟苅羽田刀弁). His full sister is {{ill|Futajiiri-hime|ja|両道入姫命}} (ふたじいりひめのみこと, also known as 石衝毘売命), the mother of the 14th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Chūai|en|Emperor Chūai|qid=Q179971|lt=Chūai Tennō}}.

His children include {{ill|Iwakia Betsuō|ja|磐城別王|lt=Ishikyoubetsu-Ō}} (いわきわけ, also known as 伊波智和希) and {{ill|Mizuhanarō-hime|ja|水歯郎媛}} (みずはのいらつめ), who is recorded as the mother of the consort of the 12th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Keikō|en|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723|lt=Keikō Tennō}}, {{ill|Gohyakuno Ōjo|ja|五百野皇女}}.

== Names ==
The written form of his name varies among ancient texts. In this article the form “磐衝別命” is uniformly used.
* '''Ihatokuhowaki''' (伊波都久和希) – according to an apocryphal text from {{ill|Jōgūki|ja|上宮記|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10867356}}<ref group="原" name="上宮">『{{ill|Shaku Nihongi|en|Shaku Nihongi|qid=Q2710483|lt=Shaku Nihonki}}』巻13 述義9 第17所収『{{ill|Jōgūki|ja|上宮記|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10867356}}』逸文 ([{{NDLDC|991097/354}} {{ill|Kokushi Taikei Volume 7|ja|国史大系 第7巻}}] (経済雑誌社, 1897–1901, 国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション) panels 354–355).</ref>
* '''Ishikyoubetsu-Ō''' (石衝別王) – as recorded in {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}.
* '''Iwattsukuwake no Mikoto''' (磐衝別命) – as found in {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} and {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|de|Shinsen Shōjiroku|fr|Shinsen shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録|ko|신찬성씨록|ru|Синсэн сёдзироку|zh|新撰姓氏錄|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}<ref group="原" name="新撰姓氏録 羽咋">『{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|de|Shinsen Shōjiroku|fr|Shinsen shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録|ko|신찬성씨록|ru|Синсэн сёдзироку|zh|新撰姓氏錄|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}』右京皇別 羽咋公条 ([{{NDLDC|1879557/77}} {{ill|Gunsho Ruijū Volume 16|ja|群書類従 第十六輯}}] (経済雑誌社, 1898–1902, 国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション) panel 77).</ref>
* “Iwattsukuwake” (磐撞別命) – as it appears in the “{{ill|Kujiki|ar|كجيكي|fa|کوجیکی (سندای کوجی هونگی)|fr|Kujiki|id|Kujiki|it|Kujiki|ja|先代旧事本紀|ko|선대구사본기|pt|Kujiki|ru|Кудзики|uk|Кудзікі|vi|Cựu sự kỷ|zh|先代舊事本紀|qid=Q2716751}}” section of {{ill|Kujiki|ar|كجيكي|fa|کوجیکی (سندای کوجی هونگی)|fr|Kujiki|id|Kujiki|it|Kujiki|ja|先代旧事本紀|ko|선대구사본기|pt|Kujiki|ru|Кудзики|uk|Кудзікі|vi|Cựu sự kỷ|zh|先代舊事本紀|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kyuujihonki}}<ref group="原" name="天皇本紀">『{{ill|Kujiki|ar|كجيكي|fa|کوجیکی (سندای کوجی هونگی)|fr|Kujiki|id|Kujiki|it|Kujiki|ja|先代旧事本紀|ko|선대구사본기|pt|Kujiki|ru|Кудзики|uk|Кудзікі|vi|Cựu sự kỷ|zh|先代舊事本紀|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kyuujihonki}}』「{{ill|Kujiki|ar|كجيكي|fa|کوجیکی (سندای کوجی هونگی)|fr|Kujiki|id|Kujiki|it|Kujiki|ja|先代旧事本紀|ko|선대구사본기|pt|Kujiki|ru|Кудзики|uk|Кудзікі|vi|Cựu sự kỷ|zh|先代舊事本紀|qid=Q2716751}}」, 垂仁天皇条 ([{{NDLDC|991097/183}} {{ill|Kokushi Taikei Volume 7|ja|国史大系 第7巻}}] (経済雑誌社, 1897–1901, 国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション) panel 183).</ref>
* “Ishikyoubetsu no Mikoto” (石衝別命) – as it appears in the “{{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|ja|国造本紀|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q133833194}}” section of {{ill|Kujiki|ar|كجيكي|fa|کوجیکی (سندای کوجی هونگی)|fr|Kujiki|id|Kujiki|it|Kujiki|ja|先代旧事本紀|ko|선대구사본기|pt|Kujiki|ru|Кудзики|uk|Кудзікі|vi|Cựu sự kỷ|zh|先代舊事本紀|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kyuujihonki}}<ref group="原" name="国造本紀 羽咋">『{{ill|Kujiki|ar|كجيكي|fa|کوجیکی (سندای کوجی هونگی)|fr|Kujiki|id|Kujiki|it|Kujiki|ja|先代旧事本紀|ko|선대구사본기|pt|Kujiki|ru|Кудзики|uk|Кудзікі|vi|Cựu sự kỷ|zh|先代舊事本紀|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kyuujihonki}}』「{{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|ja|国造本紀|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q133833194}}」羽咋国造条 ([{{NDLDC|991097/221}} {{ill|Kokushi Taikei Volume 7|ja|国史大系 第7巻}}] (経済雑誌社, 1897–1901, 国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション) panel 221).</ref><ref group="原" name="加我">『{{ill|Kujiki|ar|كجيكي|fa|کوجیکی (سندای کوجی هونگی)|fr|Kujiki|id|Kujiki|it|Kujiki|ja|先代旧事本紀|ko|선대구사본기|pt|Kujiki|ru|Кудзики|uk|Кудзікі|vi|Cựu sự kỷ|zh|先代舊事本紀|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kyuujihonki}}』「{{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|ja|国造本紀|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q133833194}}」加我国造条 ([{{NDLDC|991097/221}} {{ill|Kokushi Taikei Volume 7|ja|国史大系 第7巻}}] (経済雑誌社, 1897–1901, 国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション) panel 221).</ref>

== Genealogy ==
<small>（The genealogy is based primarily on the first appearance in {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}, with other texts indicated in parentheses）</small>

He is the tenth son of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Suinin Tennō}} and the daughter of Yamashiro Ōkuni Fuchisoku, known as {{ill|Kamuhatotobe|ja|綺戸辺}} (かむはたとべ, 弟苅羽田刀弁). His full sister is {{ill|Futajiiri-hime|ja|両道入姫命|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q65248127}} (ふたじいりひめのみこと, also known as 石衝毘売命), the mother of the 14th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Chūai|en|Emperor Chūai|qid=Q179971|lt=Chūai Tennō}}.

His children include {{ill|Iwakia Betsuō|ja|磐城別王|lt=Ishikyoubetsu-Ō}} (いわきわけ, also rendered as 伊波智和希) and {{ill|Mizuhanarō-hime|ja|水歯郎媛}} (みずはのいらつめ), who is noted in the {{ill|Emperor Keikō|en|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723|lt=Keikō Tennō}} account as the mother of the consort {{ill|Gohyakuno Ōjo|ja|五百野皇女}}.

According to the apocryphal text of {{ill|Jōgūki|ja|上宮記|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10867356}} (as included in {{ill|Shaku Nihongi|en|Shaku Nihongi|qid=Q2710483|lt=Shaku Nihonki}}), a genealogy of Iwattsukuwake no Mikoto’s descendants is recorded; his fifth-generation descendant, {{ill|Furihime|ja|振媛|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q28415396}}, married {{ill|Hikoushi no Ōkimi|ja|彦主人王|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11487892}} and bore {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|qid=Q349277|lt=Keitai Tennō}} (referred to as Kofutō Taikō Ō, the 26th emperor).

The {{ill|Kujiki|ar|كجيكي|fa|کوجیکی (سندای کوجی هونگی)|fr|Kujiki|id|Kujiki|it|Kujiki|ja|先代旧事本紀|ko|선대구사본기|pt|Kujiki|ru|Кудзики|uk|Кудзікі|vi|Cựu sự kỷ|zh|先代舊事本紀|qid=Q2716751}} section of {{ill|Kujiki|ar|كجيكي|fa|کوجیکی (سندای کوجی هونگی)|fr|Kujiki|id|Kujiki|it|Kujiki|ja|先代旧事本紀|ko|선대구사본기|pt|Kujiki|ru|Кудзики|uk|Кудзікі|vi|Cựu sự kỷ|zh|先代舊事本紀|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kyuujihonki}} recounts an alternative tradition in which the consort of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Suinin Tennō}}, who bore him a son, was the daughter of {{ill|Tanba-no-Michinushi-no-Mikoto|ja|丹波道主王|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 丹波道主命|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11368587}}, named {{ill|Matono-hime|ja|真砥野媛}}, and that he had a half-sibling, {{ill|Ojiwake no mikoto|ja|祖別命|zh|祖別命|qid=Q11620549}}. Furthermore, the “{{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|ja|国造本紀|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q133833194}}” relates that a fourth-generation descendant, known as Ōyhiko-kun, is recorded.

== Tomb ==
[[File:Ootsuka (Hakui-nanatsuka).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{ill|Hakui Shrine|ja|羽咋神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11610064}} ({{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|en|Ishikawa Prefecture|qid=Q131281|lt=Ishikawa Prefecture}}, {{ill|Hakui, Ishikawa|en|Hakui, Ishikawa|qid=Q822585|lt=Hakui City}})]]
The tomb is designated at the '''Iwattsukuwake no Mikoto Tomb''' (磐衝別命墓, いわつくわけのみことのはか, {{ウィキ座標|36|53|50.64|N|136|46|46.09|E|region:JP-17|位置|name=磐衝別命墓}}) located within the precincts of {{ill|Hakui Shrine|ja|羽咋神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11610064}} in {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|en|Ishikawa Prefecture|qid=Q131281|lt=Ishikawa Prefecture}}, {{ill|Hakui, Ishikawa|en|Hakui, Ishikawa|qid=Q822585|lt=Hakui City}}.<ref name="陵墓">宮内省諸陵寮編 [{{NDLDC|1237123/9}} 『陵墓要覧』] (1934, 国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション) panel 9.</ref> The official form as recognized by the Imperial Household Agency is that of a {{ill|Circular Tomb|ja|円墳|simple|Round Kofun|zh|圓墳|qid=Q11394747}}. The site is also known by names such as “Hakui Goryōzan Kofun.”

Although his tomb is not mentioned in historical records, in Taishō 6 (1917) it was officially designated by the {{ill|Ministry of the Imperial Household|en|Ministry of the Imperial Household|qid=Q8193428|lt=Imperial Household Ministry}} (now the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ar|وكالة رعاية القصر الإمبراطوري|ca|Agència de la Casa Imperial|de|Kaiserliches Hofamt|es|Agencia de la Casa Imperial|fa|دفتر خاندان امپراتوری|fr|Agence impériale|ha|Hukumar Kula da Gidajen Daular|he|סוכנות משק הבית הקיסרי|hr|Uprava japanskog carskog dvora|id|Badan Rumah Tangga Kekaisaran|it|Agenzia della Casa Imperiale|ja|宮内庁|ko|일본 궁내청|lt|Imperatoriškosios šeimos agentūra|min|Badan Rumah Tanggo Kakaisaran|ms|Agensi Rumah Tangga Imperial|nl|Japans hof|pl|Agencja Dworu Cesarskiego|pt|Agência da Casa Imperial|ru|Управление Императорского двора Японии|simple|Imperial Household Agency|th|สำนักพระราชวังหลวง (ญี่ปุ่น)|tr|İmparatorluk Sarayı Ajansı|uk|Управління Імператорського двору Японії|vi|Cơ quan nội chính Hoàng gia Nhật Bản|zh|宫内厅|qid=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}}) as his official tomb. The kofun is believed to be a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|qid=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun}} approximately 100 meters in length, constructed around the mid-5th century.<ref name="現地">現地説明板。</ref>

Adjacent to the tomb is a {{ill|Circular Tomb|ja|円墳|simple|Round Kofun|zh|圓墳|qid=Q11394747}} (Hakui Ōtanizuka Kofun), which was designated in Taishō 6 (1917) as the tomb of his son, {{ill|Iwakia Betsuō Tomb|ja|磐城別王墓|qid=Q140446118}}.<ref name="陵墓"/><ref name="現地"/>

An alternative tradition from the legend of {{ill|Mio Shrine|ja|水尾神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11548449}} (in {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Shiga|af|Shiga-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Shiga|ar|شيغا (محافظة)|az|Şiqa prefekturası|azb|شیقا اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Shiga|be|Сіга (прэфектура)|bg|Шига|bn|শিগা প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|br|Prefedelezh Shiga|ca|Prefectura de Shiga|cdo|Shiga-gâing|ce|Сига (префектура)|ceb|Shiga-ken|ckb|پارێزگای شیگا|cs|Prefektura Šiga|cy|Shiga (talaith)|da|Shiga-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Shiga|eo|Gubernio Ŝiga|es|Prefectura de Shiga|et|Shiga prefektuur|eu|Shiga (prefektura)|fa|استان شیگا|fi|Shigan prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Shiga|frr|Shiga (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Shiga|gl|Prefectura de Shiga|hak|Shiga-yen|he|שיגה (מחוז)|hr|Shiga (prefektura)|hu|Siga prefektúra|hy|Սիգա (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Shiga|ilo|Prepektura ti Shiga|it|Prefettura di Shiga|ja|滋賀県|jv|Préfèktur Shiga|ka|სიგის პრეფექტურა|ko|시가현|la|Shigaënsis|lt|Šigos prefektūra|lv|Sigas prefektūra|mk|Шига (префектура)|mn|Шига муж|mni|ꯁꯤꯒꯥ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|शिगा प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Shiga|ne|सिगा|nl|Shiga (prefectuur)|no|Shiga (prefektur)|os|Сигæ|pl|Prefektura Shiga|pnb|ضلع شیگا|pt|Shiga|ro|Prefectura Shiga|ru|Сига|sco|Shiga Prefectur|se|Shiga prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Shiga|si|ෂිගා ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Shiga Prefecture|sk|Šiga (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Шига|su|Préféktur Shiga|sv|Shiga prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Shiga|tg|Устони Шига|th|จังหวัดชิงะ|tl|Prepektura ng Shiga|tr|Shiga|tt|Сига (префектура)|uk|Префектура Сіґа|ur|شیگا پریفیکچر|vi|Shiga|war|Shiga (prefektura)|wuu|滋贺县|zh|滋贺县|zh_classical|滋賀縣|zh_min_nan|Siga-koān|zh_yue|滋賀縣|qid=Q131358|lt=Shiga Prefecture}}, {{ill|Takashima, Shiga|en|Takashima, Shiga|qid=Q845794|lt=Takashima City}}) states that Iwattsukuwake no Mikoto came to reside in this area to study the Tensei Shintō of {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|猿田彦|lt=Sarutahiko}} no Mikoto, and that he died here. Consequently, his son, Iwakia Betsuō, is said to have buried him on Mount Mio. In the wooded hills behind the shrine remain several group kofun (the Haido Kofun Group) from the 6th century, one of which—the Imperial Prince Mound—is traditionally regarded as the tomb of the progenitor of the Mio clan.

== Descendants ==
=== Clans ===
In the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}, Iwattsukuwake no Mikoto is described as “the progenitor of the Mio clan,” and in the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} as “the progenitor of the Hakui and Mio clans,” which are recorded as his descendant clans.
* Mio Clan (三尾氏)  
  A regional powerful clan that held sway from northern Ōmi to the Hokuriku region.<ref name="三尾">『{{ill|Nihon Kodai Shizoku Jinmei Jiten|ja|日本古代氏族人名辞典 普及版|qid=DELETED_QID}}』, 三尾氏項.</ref> Their stronghold is estimated to have been in Miou Township of Takashima District, {{ill|Ōmi Province|en|Ōmi Province|qid=Q843882|lt=Ōmi Province}} (present-day near the Miou-ri area of {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Shiga|af|Shiga-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Shiga|ar|شيغا (محافظة)|az|Şiqa prefekturası|azb|شیقا اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Shiga|be|Сіга (прэфектура)|bg|Шига|bn|শিগা প্রশাসনিক Prefecture}}, {{ill|Takashima, Shiga|en|Takashima, Shiga|qid=Q845794|lt=Takashima City}}, Azumigawa, or in Sakaigun of Echizen Province (present-day near Awara City in {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|en|Fukui Prefecture|qid=Q133879|lt=Fukui Prefecture}}).
  According to the {{ill|Jōgūki|ja|上宮記|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10867356}} apocryphal text, the clan was connected with the origin of {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|qid=Q349277|lt=Keitai Tennō}}, as two of his consorts are said to have come from this lineage.
* Hakui Clan (羽咋氏)  
  A local powerful clan that flourished in the Hakui District of {{ill|Noto Province|en|Noto Province|qid=Q1047671|lt=Noto Province}}, in the area of present-day {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|en|Ishikawa Prefecture|qid=Q131281|lt=Ishikawa Prefecture}} around Hakui City. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|de|Shinsen Shōjiroku|fr|Shinsen shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録|ko|신찬성씨록|ru|Синсэн сёдзироку|zh|新撰姓氏錄|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}, it is recorded under the Right Capital Imperial Edition as “{{ill|Hakui Kō|ja|羽咋公}}” and is mentioned as succeeding the son of Iwattsukuwake no Mikoto.<ref group="原" name="新撰姓氏録 羽咋"/> As suggested in the “{{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|ja|国造本紀|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q133833194}}”, it is presumed to be the clan of Hakui Kunizō; however, since it does not appear in Nara period documents, its political prominence is believed to have declined early.

=== National Governors ===
Regarding the national governors ({{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|en|Kuni no miyatsuko|qid=Q2483673|lt=Kuni-zukuri}}) associated with Iwattsukuwake no Mikoto, two figures are attested:
* {{ill|Kaga Kunizukuri|ja|加我国造}} (かがのくにのみやつこ, 賀我国造)  
  Presumed to have governed the area of Kaga District in {{ill|Kaga Province|en|Kaga Province|qid=Q907469|lt=Kaga Province}} (present-day the region of {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|en|Ishikawa Prefecture|qid=Q131281|lt=Ishikawa Prefecture}}’s Kahoku District).<ref>『国造制の研究 -史料編・論考編-』 (八木書店, 2013) p. 217.</ref> In the “{{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|ja|国造本紀|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q133833194}}”, it is recorded that during the reign of Emperor Yuryaku, the fourth-generation descendant, Ōyhiko-kun, was appointed as the first national governor.
* {{ill|Hakui Kunizukuri|ja|羽咋国造}} (はくいのくにのみやつこ)  
  Presumed to have governed the Hakui District of {{ill|Noto Province|en|Noto Province|qid=Q1047671|lt=Noto Province}} (present-day the area of {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|en|Ishikawa Prefecture|qid=Q131281|lt=Ishikawa Prefecture}} surrounding Hakui City).<ref>『国造制の研究 -史料編・論考編-』 (八木書店, 2013) p. 220.</ref> According to the “{{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|ja|国造本紀|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q133833194}}”, he is recorded as having been appointed as the first national governor by Iwakia Betsuō, the son of Iwattsukuwake no Mikoto.

== Related Sites ==
{{GeoGroup}}
[[File:Hakui-jinja haiden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{ill|Hakui Shrine|ja|羽咋神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11610064}} ({{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|en|Ishikawa Prefecture|qid=Q131281|lt=Ishikawa Prefecture}}, {{ill|Hakui, Ishikawa|en|Hakui, Ishikawa|qid=Q822585|lt=Hakui City}})]]
* {{ill|Hakui Shrine|ja|羽咋神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11610064}} (はくいじんじゃ) – A {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}}, formerly a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qid=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q90139226|qq= 近代社格制度}}. Its principal enshrined deity is Iwattsukuwake no Mikoto. Tradition holds that a descendant known as Hakui-kun enshrined his ancestral deity here. The precincts include the ancient tomb designated as Iwattsukuwake no Mikoto’s tomb.
* The annual event held at the shrine, the {{ill|Karadoyama Shinjitsu Sumo|ja|唐戸山神事相撲}} (designated as an intangible folk cultural property by Hakui City), is said to have originated from the sumo held on his memorial day, September 25, in honor of his benevolent governance. According to local legend, the place name “Hakui” derives from an incident in which he shot down a vicious bird that tormented his subjects, the feathers of which were then consumed by three dogs (alternatively, one theory attributes the name to the legend of {{ill|Ōkuninushi|abstract|Q276944|ca|Ōkuninushi|es|Ōkuninushi|fa|اوکونینوشی|fr|Ōkuninushi|hu|Ókuninusi|id|Ookuninushi|it|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|ko|오오쿠니누시|mni|ꯑꯣꯀꯨꯅꯤꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Ōkuninushi|pt|Ookuninushi|ru|Окунинуси|simple|Ōkuninushi|sr|Okuninuši|sv|Ōkuninushi|tr|Ōkuninushi|uk|Окунінуші|vi|Ōkuninushi|zh|大國主|qid=Q276944}}). It is also recorded that his wife was known as {{ill|Mitarashi-hime|ja|三足比咩命|qid=Q140446119}}.
* In the vicinity of the shrine, including the tomb of Iwattsukuwake no Mikoto and the tomb of his son {{ill|Iwakia Betsuō Tomb|ja|磐城別王墓|qid=Q140446118}}, there are seven mounds ({{ill|Hakui-nanatsuka|ja|羽咋七塚|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11610061}}) associated with his legacy.<ref name="現地"/><ref name="羽咋神社"/>
[[File:Mio-jinja (Takashima) shaden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{ill|Mio Shrine|ja|水尾神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11548449}} ({{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Shiga|af|Shiga-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Shiga|ar|شيغا (محافظة)|az|Şiqa prefekturası|azb|شیقا اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Shiga|be|Сіга (прэфектура)|bg|Шига|bn|শিগা প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|br|Prefedelezh Shiga|ca|Prefectura de Shiga|cdo|Shiga-gâing|ce|Сига (префектура)|ceb|Shiga-ken|ckb|پارێزگای شیگا|cs|Prefektura Šiga|cy|Shiga (talaith)|da|Shiga-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Shiga|eo|Gubernio Ŝiga|es|Prefectura de Shiga|et|Shiga prefektuur|eu|Shiga (prefektura)|fa|استان شیگا|fi|Shigan prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Shiga|frr|Shiga (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Shiga|gl|Prefectura de Shiga|hak|Shiga-yen|he|שיגה (מחוז)|hr|Shiga (prefektura)|hu|Siga prefektúra|hy|Սիգա (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Shiga|ilo|Prepektura ti Shiga|it|Prefettura di Shiga|ja|滋賀県|jv|Préfèktur Shiga|ka|სიგის პრეფექტურა|ko|시가현|la|Shigaënsis|lt|Šigos prefektūra|lv|Sigas prefektūra|mk|Шига (префектура)|mn|Шига муж|mni|ꯁꯤꯒꯥ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|शिगा प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Shiga|ne|सिगा|nl|Shiga (prefectuur)|no|Shiga (prefektur)|os|Сигæ|pl|Prefektura Shiga|pnb|ضلع شیگا|pt|Shiga|ro|Prefectura Shiga|ru|Сига|sco|Shiga Prefectur|se|Shiga prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Shiga|si|ෂිගා ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Shiga Prefecture|sk|Šiga (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Шига|su|Préféktur Shiga|sv|Shiga prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Shiga|tg|Устони Шига|th|จังหวัดชิงะ|tl|Prepektura ng Shiga|tr|Shiga|tt|Сига (префектура)|uk|Префектура Сіґа|ur|شیگا پریفیکچر|vi|Shiga|war|Shiga (prefektura)|wuu|滋贺县|zh|滋贺县|zh_classical|滋賀縣|zh_min_nan|Siga-koān|zh_yue|滋賀縣|qid=Q131358|lt=Shiga Prefecture}}, {{ill|Takashima, Shiga|en|Takashima, Shiga|qid=Q845794|lt=Takashima City}})]]
* {{ill|Mio Shrine|ja|水尾神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11548449}} (みおじんじゃ) – A {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}}, formerly a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qid=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q90139226|qq= 近代社格制度}}. Its enshrined deities are Iwattsukuwake no Mikoto and the deity of Mitarashi ({{ill|Furihime|ja|振媛|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q28415396}}). According to its tradition, Iwattsukuwake no Mikoto visited this area to study the Tensei Shintō of {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|猿田彦|lt=Sarutahiko}} no Mikoto and died here; consequently, his son, Iwakia Betsuō, buried him on Mount Mio and established the shrine. The shrine also venerates Mitarashi, who is said to have given birth to {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|qid=Q349277|lt=Keitai Tennō}}.
* {{ill|Ōminato Shrine|ja|大湊神社|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135579299}} (おおみなとじんじゃ) – A Shikinaisha. Historical records indicate that Iwattsukuwake no Mikoto was once enshrined here.
* {{ill|Fukuhi Shrine|ja|布久比神社}} (ふくいじんじゃ) – A Shikinaisha which enshrines Iwattsukuwake no Mikoto as “{{ill|Iwa tsuku wake no Mikoto|ja|岩衝別命|qid=Q11587884}}.”
